results.title: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra warns of cryptocurrency risks to India's monetary sovereignty
results.subject: economy
results.why_in_news: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra warned of cryptocurrency risks to India's monetary sovereignty while expressing support for distributed ledger technology and tokenisation.
results.fact_box: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra spoke at the Kautilya Economic Conclave on October 3, 2026. He linked rising public debt and hardening bond yields to increased government and private spending on artificial intelligence.
results.mains_question: Discuss the implications of decentralized cryptocurrencies on a nation's monetary sovereignty and the role of the central bank in regulating digital assets.

results.title: Revanth Reddy directs state departments to create online safety framework for children
results.subject: social_justice
results.why_in_news: A. Revanth Reddy directed state departments to create an online safety framework for children in collaboration with the High Court and State Legal Services Authority (SLSA).
results.fact_box: The directive was issued during a conference in Hyderabad where Arjun Ram Meghwal emphasized providing legal support for victims. The framework aims to establish online safety protocols for children.
results.mains_question: Discuss the necessity of a robust legal and technological framework to ensure the online safety of children in India.

results.title: Gujarat becomes second state to receive presidential assent for Uniform Civil Code Bill 2026
results.subject: polity
results.why_in_news: Gujarat became the second state after Uttarakhand to receive presidential assent for its Uniform Civil Code (UCC) Bill 2026, which unifies personal laws for marriage, divorce, and succession.
results.fact_box: The Gujarat UCC Bill 2026 prohibits polygamy and sets the marriage age at 21 for men and 18 for women.
results.mains_question: Discuss the constitutional challenges and social implications of implementing a Uniform Civil Code while preserving the customary rights of Scheduled Tribes.

results.title: Nirmala Sitharaman, Anant Ambani join to launch ₹1 lakh crore Rayalaseema Rising project
results.subject: agriculture
results.why_in_news: Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman and Reliance Industries' Anant Ambani joined CM N. Chandrababu Naidu to launch the ₹1 lakh crore Rayalaseema Rising project in Andhra Pradesh.
results.fact_box: The Rayalaseema Rising project is a ₹1 lakh crore initiative to transform 10 districts of Andhra Pradesh into a global horticulture centre. The launch included laying the foundation stone for the Indian School of Agriculture.
results.mains_question: Discuss how large-scale private-public partnerships in horticulture can drive regional economic development and agricultural modernization in India.

results.title: World food prices hit nearly four-year high as logistics disruptions and El Nino persist
results.subject: agriculture
results.why_in_news: The UN's Food and Agriculture Organization reported that world food prices hit a nearly four-year high in September due to logistics disruptions and El Niño weather patterns.
results.fact_box: The FAO Food Price Index averaged 136.0 points in September. Prices for sugar reached an 18-month high and wheat reached a three-year peak due to disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz and Black Sea.
results.mains_question: Analyze how geopolitical disruptions in maritime corridors and climate change phenomena like El Niño contribute to global food insecurity and price volatility.

results.title: Jessica Watkins becomes first Black woman to lead crew to orbit in record flight
results.subject: science_tech
results.why_in_news: SpaceX launched a crew to the International Space Station (ISS) led by Jessica Watkins, the first Black woman to lead a crew to orbit, setting a U.S. speed record.
results.fact_box: The mission involved four crew members: Jessica Watkins (NASA commander), Luke Delaney, Joshua Kutryk, and Sergey Teteryatnikov. The flight lasted eight hours and launched from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station.
results.mains_question: Discuss the significance of private-public partnerships in expanding human space exploration and the socio-cultural implications of diversifying space missions.

results.title: 87.7% of individual equity derivatives traders lost Rs 91,685 crore in FY26
results.subject: economy
results.why_in_news: SEBI data revealed that 87.7% of individual equity derivatives traders incurred losses of Rs 91,685 crore in FY26, highlighting the risks of high-leverage trading.
results.fact_box: In FY26, 87.7% of individual equity derivatives traders lost a total of Rs 91,685 crore, with an average loss of Rs 1.17 lakh. Options trading accounted for 92% of these losses, while SIP contributions reached a record Rs 32,297 crore in August 2026.
results.mains_question: Discuss the risks associated with retail participation in equity derivatives and suggest measures to enhance investor protection in the Indian capital markets.

results.title: Netherlands Minister Silvio Erkens visits Bengaluru to explore agricultural collaboration with 18 businesses
results.subject: ir
results.why_in_news: Netherlands Minister Silvio Erkens visited Bengaluru to explore agricultural collaboration with 18 businesses, focusing on water management and climate-resilient seeds.
results.fact_box: Silvio Erkens, the Netherlands Minister for Food Security, Fisheries and Horticulture, visited Bengaluru to discuss cooperation with the Union government, Maharashtra, and the India-Netherlands Seed Forum. The collaboration targets water management, precision irrigation, and climate-resilient seeds.
results.mains_question: Discuss how international agricultural collaborations can enhance India's climate-resilient farming and water management strategies for smallholder farmers.

results.title: MSF warns $28,000 annual cost limits access to Gilead's HIV prevention injection
results.subject: social_justice
results.why_in_news: MSF warned that the $28,000 annual cost of Gilead's lenacapavir injection limits access to HIV prevention, despite its efficacy in clinical trials.
results.fact_box: Gilead Sciences developed lenacapavir, a twice-yearly injection for HIV prevention. A 2024 trial involving over 2,000 women in South Africa and Uganda showed zero infections.
results.mains_question: Discuss the challenges of balancing pharmaceutical innovation with equitable access to life-saving medicines in low-income countries.

results.title: Adani Green to build world's largest single-location battery storage at Khavda, Gujarat
results.subject: economy
results.why_in_news: Adani Green Energy Ltd (AGEL) expanded its Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) capacity at Khavda, Gujarat, to 6.63 GWh, making it the world's largest single-location installation.
results.fact_box: The Khavda BESS facility uses lithium-ion battery technology integrated with Energy Management Systems (EMS) and automated telemetry. It accounts for over 50% of India's total operational BESS capacity of 12.6 GWh.
results.mains_question: Discuss the significance of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) in achieving India's goal of a resilient and low-carbon power grid.

results.title: Pollution, unregulated construction and climate change threaten Dal Lake's deteriorating ecosystem
results.subject: environment
results.why_in_news: Dal Lake in Srinagar faces an ecological crisis due to untreated sewage, plastic waste, and unregulated construction, threatening the local ecosystem and livelihoods.
results.fact_box: Dal Lake in Srinagar, Indian-administered Kashmir, is experiencing ecosystem deterioration from untreated sewage, plastic waste, and weed growth. Land encroachment and rising temperatures are actively reducing the lake's surface area.
results.mains_question: Discuss the ecological and socio-economic impacts of urban encroachment and pollution on high-altitude lake ecosystems like Dal Lake.

results.title: Wedding gifts worth Rs 10 lakh exempt from tax under Section 56(2)(x)
results.subject: economy
results.why_in_news: Gaurav Singh Parmar of Fincorpit Consulting clarified that wedding gifts up to Rs 10 lakh are exempt from tax under Section 56(2)(x) of the Income Tax Act.
results.fact_box: Under Section 56(2)(x) of the Income Tax Act, wedding gifts up to Rs 10 lakh are exempt from tax. Gifts from non-relatives exceeding Rs 50,000 in a financial year are generally taxable as 'Income from Other Sources'.
results.mains_question: Discuss the implications of taxing gifts and assets received from non-relatives on the scope of 'Income from Other Sources' and tax evasion in India.

results.title: Tamil Nadu's first booth-less toll plaza opens with multi-lane free flow system
results.subject: science_tech
results.why_in_news: The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) launched Tamil Nadu's first booth-less toll plaza at Paranur using a multi-lane free flow system to reduce congestion.
results.fact_box: The Paranur toll plaza on the Chennai - Tiruchi National Highway is the first booth-less facility in Tamil Nadu. It utilizes a multi-lane free flow system to process 46,500 daily vehicles.
results.mains_question: Discuss how the implementation of multi-lane free flow toll systems contributes to infrastructure efficiency and the digital transformation of public services in India.

results.title: Karnataka to allocate ₹25 crore for up to 100 start-ups under ‘Government First’ initiative
results.subject: economy
results.why_in_news: Karnataka announced the ‘Government First’ initiative to provide financial support to 100 start-ups for pilot deployments in technology sectors.
results.fact_box: The initiative is part of the Elevate programme under the Karnataka Startup Policy 2025–30. It allocates a total of ₹25 crore to support up to 100 start-ups over a three-year period, with individual grants of up to ₹25 lakh.
results.mains_question: Discuss how state-led startup policies like Karnataka's 'Government First' initiative can foster innovation and bridge the gap between technology development and public service delivery.

results.title: Andhra Pradesh forms high-powered committee to investigate attacks, murders and harassment of journalists
results.subject: polity
results.why_in_news: The Andhra Pradesh government issued GO 1913 to constitute a high-powered committee to investigate attacks, murders, and harassment of journalists following demands for safety and benefits.
results.fact_box: The committee is led by the State Home Minister and Kolusu Parthasarathi. It includes representatives from journalist associations and the Commissioner of Information and Public Relations to address safety and accreditation issues.
results.mains_question: Discuss the importance of ensuring the safety and freedom of the press as a cornerstone of a functioning democracy in India.

results.title: India records 759.4 mm rainfall, fourth lowest since 2001 as monsoon ends
results.subject: geography
results.why_in_news: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) reported that India received only 87.4% of its long period average rainfall for the 2026 monsoon season, marking the fourth lowest rainfall since 2001.
results.fact_box: India recorded 759.4 mm of rainfall from June 1 to September 30, 2026. This represents a 13 per cent deficit compared to the long period average of 868.6 mm.
results.mains_question: Analyze the impact of increasing rainfall variability and monsoon deficits on India's food security and water management strategies.

results.title: Keralam needs 27 GW renewable capacity to reach 100% goal by 2040
results.subject: science_tech
results.why_in_news: WRI India released a study in Thiruvananthapuram stating Kerala requires 27 GW of renewable capacity and ₹64,890 crore investment to achieve a 100% renewable energy goal by 2040.
results.fact_box: The study, titled 'Pathways for Kerala’s Clean Energy Transition,' was presented at a Kerala State Electricity Board workshop. It highlights that currently, 60% of Kerala's electricity demand is met by thermal power plants located in other states, while renewable sources (wind, solar, small hydro) contribute only 7%.
results.mains_question: Discuss the challenges and financial requirements involved in transitioning a state's power grid to 100% renewable energy by 2040.

results.title: Sebi not considering stock exchange self-listing proposals after NSE market debut
results.subject: economy

results.title: Supreme Court to Examine Threat to Press Freedom in **The Hindu** Case
results.subject: polity
results.why_in_news: The Supreme Court agreed to examine a 2003 case involving *The Hindu* and Tamil Nadu’s legislative privilege to determine if Article 194(3) can be used to limit press freedom under Article 19(1)(a).
results.fact_box: Senior journalist Seema Chishti moved an application to intervene in a case where the Tamil Nadu Assembly accused *The Hindu* of breaching privileges. The Supreme Court scheduled the matter before a seven-judge Bench for October 6, 2026.
results.mains_question: Critically examine the conflict between legislative privileges and the fundamental right to freedom of the press in the Indian constitutional framework.

results.title: Coast Guard nabs ₹3,000 crore drug haul from Iranian boat off Lakshadweep
results.subject: security

results.title: Delhi Police files 398-page chargesheet in minor’s bus rape, Supreme Court takes notice
results.subject: security

results.mains_question: Discuss the systemic challenges in ensuring the safety of women in public transport and the role of judicial oversight in addressing law enforcement lapses.

results.title: DDX39A Protein Unwinds Viral RNA, Slows Parkinson’s-Linked Clumps
results.subject: science_tech
results.why_in_news: Scientists at CSIR-CCMB discovered that the DDX39A protein acts as a defense mechanism by unwinding viral RNA to slow the formation of alpha-synuclein clumps linked to Parkinson’s disease.
results.fact_box: Researchers at the CSIR-Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology (CCMB) identified that RNA viruses (influenza and SARS-CoV-2) accelerate alpha-synuclein aggregation. The DDX39A protein moves into the cytoplasm during infection to unwind viral RNA structures and mitigate protein clumping.
results.mains_question: Discuss the potential of identifying protein-mediated cellular responses to viral infections in developing targeted therapies for neurodegenerative disorders like Parkinson’s disease.

results.title: India's Defence Minister Calls for Upgrading Maritime Surveillance at Navy Conference
results.subject: security

results.mains_question: Examine the significance of maritime surveillance in ensuring India's energy security and its role as a 'First Responder' in the Indian Ocean Region.

results.title: OpenAI apologizes to Australia after AI models breach Medicare system in June

results.title: Elephants Quickly Adapt Tactics to Get Food, Study Finds
results.subject: science_tech
results.why_in_news: A study by Sydney Hope and colleagues at Hunter College revealed that Asian elephants can rapidly adapt their foraging tactics when familiar methods fail.
results.fact_box: The study was published in PLOS One on September 9, 2026, and conducted at Thailand's National Elephant Institute. Researchers observed that while elephants could adapt to new food-access methods within seconds, older elephants exhibited slower adaptation times.
results.mains_question: Discuss how understanding cognitive behavioral patterns in megafauna can inform more effective strategies for mitigating human-elephant conflict in biodiversity hotspots.

results.title: Karnataka Minister Writes to Union Chief: High-Cost Medicines Sell 70 Times Above Procurement Prices
results.subject: social_justice

results.title: Since September 2024, India's IPO market has surged with a 167% increase

results.title: SpaceX cuts Starship orbital flight short to three hours due to safety concerns
results.subject: science_tech

results.title: Telangana Fire Department discusses classifying industries into G1, G2, and G3 risk categories
results.subject: science_tech

results.mains_question: Discuss how risk-based regulatory frameworks and real-time monitoring technologies can enhance industrial safety and streamline administrative compliance in India.

results.title: ISRO and CNES are preparing to launch TRISHNA from Sriharikota in 2027
results.subject: science_tech

results.title: Supreme Court takes action on Delhi's gang-rape cases, echoes 2012 Nirbhaya failures

results.subject: science_tech

results.title: Supreme Court wants law to safeguard multi-crore court deposits - The Hindu
results.subject: polity
results.why_in_news: The Supreme Court directed the Law Commission of India to examine legislation to standardize the management of litigants' deposits during pending appeals.
results.fact_box: Justices P.S. Narasimha and Alok Aradhe highlighted that inconsistent rules lead to deposited money being entangled in various financial instruments with differing interest rates. The court suggested the U.S. Court Registry Investment System (CRIS) model as a reference for pooling deposits into a unified scheme.
results.mains_question: Discuss the necessity of a standardized legal framework for managing court deposits to ensure transparency and reduce post-judgment litigation in the Indian judiciary.

results.title: Sabotage Attempts On India's Semiconductor Push? What Ashwini Vaishnaw Said
results.subject: science_tech
results.why_in_news: Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw warned of potential sabotage, cyber attacks, and fake news targeting India's growing semiconductor industry as it scales up production.
results.fact_box: The 2026 SEMICON India event saw participation from approximately 300 international companies. Between September 17 and September 19, 56 Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) were signed.
results.mains_question: Discuss the security challenges and geopolitical risks associated with India's ambition to become a global hub for semiconductor manufacturing.

results.title: Stanford scientists transplanted human brain tissue into mice missing most of their cortex; within months, it grew to occupy more than 90% of the space - The Times of India
results.subject: science_tech
results.why_in_news: Stanford scientists led by Sergiu Pasca successfully transplanted lab-grown human brain tissue into mice lacking most of their cerebral cortex to study human neuron development.
results.fact_box: The study, published in Nature on September 16, showed human tissue expanded to occupy over 90% of the cortical space in mice. The transplanted tissue formed functional connections with the mouse's brain and spinal cord.
results.mains_question: Discuss the ethical and scientific implications of using human-animal chimeric models in neurobiology research to understand complex neurological disorders.

results.title: Ecologists urge scientists and policymakers to study imminent ‘Super’ El Niño to prepare for the future - The Hindu
results.subject: environment
results.why_in_news: A group of 188 Indian scientists and ecologists published an appeal urging researchers to prepare for a 'Super' El Niño event expected to cause extreme heat and drought.
results.fact_box: Pacific Ocean temperatures reached +2.6°C above normal in August 2026, with projections of anomalies up to +4°C. These levels are reported to be higher than any time in the past 1,000 years based on coral core reconstructions.
results.mains_question: Discuss the impact of extreme El Niño events on India's monsoon patterns and suggest measures to mitigate the resulting agricultural and heat-related risks.
